nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Normative z-scores were computed using NOMIS; the paper notes k-fold cross-validated regression models but does not specify the regression type.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The normative values for 1344 FreeSurfer-segmented brain regions were derived from k-fold cross-validated regression models, using which participant-level normative z-scores can be generated via a freely available Python-based script (https://github.com/medicslab/NOMIS).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Martin2025.pdf.md: 2.3. MRI acquisition and normative modeling

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study analyzed multiple structural MRI measures: (1) Cortical thickness (CT) for 34 cortical regions bilaterally; (2) Whole brain volume (brainsegvol); (3) Total cerebral white matter volume (cerebralwhitemattervol); (4) Total subcortical gray matter volume (subcortgrayvol); (5) Total cortical volume (cortexvol); (6) Hippocampal gray matter volume; (7) Cerebellar gray matter volume. All measures were derived from FreeSurfer v6.0 segmentation and converted to normative z-scores via NOMIS.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: This command produces an aseg.stats file for each participant containing volumetric and cortical thickness measurements... sex differences in z-scores of gross segmentations (i.e. whole brain [brainsegvol], total cerebral white matter [cerebralwhitemattervol], total subcortical gray matter [subcortgrayvol], and total cortical thickness [cortexvol]) were first assessed using Welch's t-tests... Hippocampal and cerebellar gray matter z-scores were additionally compared across sexes
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Martin2025.pdf.md: Section 2.3. MRI acquisition and normative modeling; Section 2.4. Statistical analyses

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The NOMIS normative modeling accounted for four explanatory variables: (1) Age - participant age at scan; (2) Sex - self-reported biological sex; (3) Intracranial volume (ICV) - to control for head size; (4) Image quality - to account for scan quality variations. These covariates were used in the regression models that generated normative z-scores from the reference population of 6,909 healthy adults aged 18-100.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: The aseg.stats file for each participant was then input into the NOrmative Morphometry Image Statistics (NOMIS) software which computes normative z-scores of participant-level measurements relative to a large sample of healthy adults ages 18-100 (n=6909), accounting for age, sex, intracranial volume, and image quality
